newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Amoco in $24 bln China petchem plan-Taiwan me.
newsitem.headline: Amoco in $24 bln China petchem plan-Taiwan me.

text.p: China plans to build a 200 billion yuan (U$24 billion) petrochemical complex with Amoco Corp in Fujian province, Taiwan local media reported on Friday.

Chairman Preston Chen of the Petrochemical Industry Association of Taiwan said he had been told by Fujian governor He Guojiang that Fujian's government was participating in the multibillion-dollar project, Taipei's Commercial Times said.
Chen, who spoke to Taiwan reporters at a petrochemical conference in Tokyo, said the Fujian leader had invited Taiwan petrochemical firms to join the project, the paper reported.
The paper, which said the Fujian project would compete with nearby Taiwan's own petrochemical expansion, quoted Chen as saying he believed the mainland project was feasible.
Taiwan's giant Formosa Plastics Group 1401.TW in 1993 began building Taiwan's first private naphtha cracker, the core of a massive US$9 billion petrochemical complex due for completion in 1999.
